newsitem.title: USA: INS case in U.S. delays Hamas leader's deportation.
newsitem.headline: INS case in U.S. delays Hamas leader's deportation.

text.p: A prosecutor told a federal judge on Monday that Hamas political leader Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook must either contest or concede that he was involved in "terrorist" activities before he can be deported.
Although Abu Marzook has agreed to his deportation from the United States, he maintains he has not been involved in or supported violence and refuses to admit the allegations.

At issue is whether Abu Marzook will have to enter any kind of plea to Immigration and Naturalisation Service charges. Defence lawyers said they believed this might be part of ongoing diplomatic negotiations aimed at finding a way to deport Abu Marzook to Jordan.
In the meantime he remains in federal prison.

Last Thursday Israel withdrew its request for the extradition of Abu Marzook, 46, who has been imprisoned in New York for the last 21 months. Israel said it was dropping its request out of fear of more violence.

Now that the extradition request has been dropped, the INS is pursuing earlier efforts to have him "excluded" from the United States under a 1990 law that refuses admission to aliens engaged in or giving material support to "terrorist" activities.
Under the law, he could be sent to the country of his birth, the country of his nationality, the country he had most recently left or another that might accept him.
Abu Marzook told Reuters in an interview last week that he believed a deal had been struck in which he would be deported to Jordan.

During a hearing on Monday, prosecutors told U.S. District Judge Denise Cote she no longer had jurisdiction because extradition was not an issue and that the matter should be returned to an immigration judge.
However, Abu Marzook's lawyers urged Cote to release their client or order his immediate deportation.
"He is prepared to renounce his green card," Michael Kennedy told the judge, explaining there was no need for lengthy administrative proceedings. "He is prepared for that exclusion now."
Kennedy is also pursuing an earlier request that his client be released because the government failed to act on Israel's extradition request by a March 28 deadline.
Cote has taken the matter under advisement.
"They (prosecutors) will delay this in any way they can," Kennedy told reporters after the hearing.
"They have no respect for the law and they certainly have no respect for Palestinians."
In 1995 Israel announced it had formally asked the United States to hand over Abu Marzook, alleging he was responsible as the head of Hamas's political arm for attacks that killed scores of Israelis.
